summary: Tested the vendor job link (/v/<token>) and the resolution-OTP feature. Backend: 14/14 pytest pass (tests/test_vendor_link_otp.py). It covers the public vendor GET/resolve endpoints over HTTP on the preview URL (invalid token 404, vendor_id null 404, full details, can_resolve logic, not-accepted 400, resolved 400, wrong OTP countdown, lock after 5 with the correct OTP also rejected, correct OTP -> Resolved/resolved_via='vendor link'/timeline/hash cleared, legacy no-hash ticket issues a new OTP, missing otp 422). It also runs direct python tests with wa mocked: the assign_vendor job text has every required field plus the /v/<token> link, sent before the Accept/Reject buttons; the new token makes the old link 404 and resets the hash and attempts. WhatsApp accept stores sha256(tid:otp) and the customer message holds the matching OTP. WhatsApp resolve without an OTP or with a wrong OTP does not resolve; the correct OTP resolves. _handle_direct_reply 'DONE 000000' and 'done' do not resolve; 'Done 123456' resolves. Admin close regression is OTP-free. Frontend on the preview URL at mobile 390px: all states render (card fields, accept-note, resolve-box, OTP error 'Incorrect OTP. 4 attempt(s) left.', locked, resolved-note, invalid). The correct OTP resolves through the UI. The resident page /t/<ticket_number> still renders. Found 2 logic loopholes and 1 latency issue (below).

critical.issue: OTP lock bypass: tapping Accept again (or replying 'accept') re-runs issue_resolve_otp, which resets otp_attempts to 0 and sends a new OTP. A vendor locked after 5 wrong tries can unlock themselves and keep brute-forcing. Reproduced: attempts 5 -> 0 after accept (tests/vendor_otp_edge_probe.py).

Accept has no status or already-accepted guard. Accept on a Resolved ticket (an old WhatsApp button tap) sets the status back to Pending and issues/sends a new OTP to the resident. Reproduced: Resolved -> Pending. Accept should be idempotent: if already accepted or the status is not Open/Pending, just ack and return.

minor.issue: Responds in about 8s on a correct OTP. pipeline.resolve_by_vendor awaits wa.send_text to the group and the customer inline instead of pipeline._fire(...). The DB updates at once, but the vendor sees a spinner for 8-16s, and a slow Whapi call can push the response past proxy timeouts. Use _fire for the notifications (same for send_otp in the legacy no-hash branch).
The attempts check and the $inc are not atomic. Parallel requests can go past 5 tries. Use find_one_and_update with {otp_attempts: {$lt: 5}} plus $inc.
A Resolved/Cancelled ticket returns 'This job can only be resolved after you accept it.', which is misleading. Return a status-specific message.
Pre-existing: does not check that the sender phone matches the assigned vendor (button id has only tid).

integration_issues.issue: After a correct OTP the button spinner runs for about 8s before vendor-resolved-note appears (backend latency above).

action_items: Make WhatsApp accept idempotent: if the ticket is already vendor_accepted or not Open/Pending, do not reset otp_attempts, re-issue the OTP or change the status.
Never reset otp_attempts once locked (only an admin should unlock).
Send resolve_by_vendor notifications (and send_otp in the legacy branch) through pipeline._fire so /resolve returns at once.
Make the verify_resolve_otp attempt increment atomic.
Return a clearer error for already Resolved/Cancelled tickets on /resolve.
critical_code_review_comments: Lock bypass via re-accept (see backend critical).
resolve_by_vendor sends WhatsApp messages inline and blocks the HTTP response.
